hook: That panicked call might not be your grandson.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, dim evening kitchen in warm tungsten light against cold blue monitor glow
world: An American suburb on a weeknight today: a warm family kitchen, and somewhere else a dark room lit by monitors
through_line: one ringing phone that turns from a panic into a hang-up

cast.Grandma: a woman in her 70s, short silver hair, red cardigan, reading glasses on a beaded chain
cast.Scammer: a man in his 30s in a black hoodie and a headset, face half in shadow

props.Phone: a smartphone in a red case, its screen glowing with a plain green incoming-call circle and no words

places.Kitchen: a cozy suburban kitchen at night, wooden table, warm pendant lamp, a kettle on the stove
places.Dark room: a cramped dark room lit only by two monitors showing jagged audio waveforms

cta: Send this to your parents and grandparents tonight.

captions.hook_line: Scammers can clone a loved one's voice from a short clip. Here's the defense 🛑
captions.body: The FTC has warned that scammers use AI voice cloning in family emergency schemes: an urgent call, a request for secrecy, then money that is hard to reverse, like wire transfers, gift cards or crypto. Agree on a family safe word, and if the caller can't give it, hang up and call back on a number you know.
captions.comment_prompt: Does your family have a safe word yet?

youtube_title: The AI Voice Scam Targeting Families

sources.claim: FTC: scammers use AI to clone voices in family emergency schemes; verify by calling back a known number

blocks.narration: That panicked call might not be your grandson. Scammers can now clone a voice from a short clip posted online.

blocks.narration: The fix is low tech. Agree on a family safe word, and ask for it on any emergency call.
